title: Hong Kong Stock Exchange's Integrated Fund Platform Launches Agent Services, with Over 60 Firms Connecting the Full Fund Distribution Chain
text:
Hong Kong Stock Exchange's Integrated Fund Platform Launches Agent Services, with Over 60 Firms Connecting the Full Fund Distribution Chain — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Hong Kong Stock Exchange's Integrated Fund Platform Launches Agent Services, with Over 60 Firms Connecting the Full Fund Distribution Chain
 Add preferred source On the 28th, the Integrated Fund Platform under the Hong Kong Stock Exchange launched its platform and agent services, incorporating master distribution, agent, and administrative functions, with all core services of the platform now fully operational. The new services cover administrative management of fund unit holdings, payment and settlement cash flows, reconciliation and reporting, and use standardized due diligence files to reduce onboarding costs between distributors and fund companies. Platform participants have grown from an initial 33 to more than 60, and the fund database integrates about 2,300 authorized funds with cumulative visits of 38 million. The Securities and Futures Commission described this as a key milestone, believing it will help broaden distribution channels over the long term and attract local and cross-border capital. Key Elements 
 Hong Kong Stock Exchange Integrated Fund Platform Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission Leung Chung-kwong Christina Ngai Lau Wai-tat fund distribution transfer agency asset and wealth management The Integrated Fund Platform under the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (00388.HK) officially launched its platform and agent services on the 28th, incorporating master distribution, agent, and administrative functions in one, marking the arrival of the platform's third-phase functions following the fund database and order transmission, with all core services now fully operational. The Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) welcomed the move the same day, describing it as a key milestone in the platform's development, with the scope of services thereby greatly expanded.
 The new services target distributors and fund companies, covering administrative management of fund unit or share holdings, cash flow processing for payment and settlement, and generation of reconciliation and reports. Through unified workflows and information exchange mechanisms, the platform connects fund managers, transfer agents, distributors, and other market participants, forming a business-to-business (B2B) integrated market infrastructure to reduce market fragmentation. Starting today, distributors, including brokerage firms, can subscribe for and redeem funds on the platform on behalf of clients.
 Leung Chung-kwong, Group Chief Information Officer of HKEX, said the Integrated Fund Platform is important market infrastructure for Hong Kong's fund ecosystem. By centralizing fund distribution workflows, the goal is to enhance the operational efficiency, transparency, and scalability of the overall ecosystem while lowering operating costs. He noted that the platform advances under a "three-step" strategy: the first step was the fund database launched in December 2024, integrating information on about 2,300 SFC-authorized funds, which had recorded 38 million cumulative visits as of the end of September this year; the second step was the order transmission service launched in July 2025; and the third step is the platform and agent services launched this time.
 On role positioning, Lau Wai-tat, Head of Fund Platform at HKEX, explained that the platform will assume the function of a "master distributor," inviting fund companies to join and offer products, then integrating resources from multiple parties so that distributors can access multiple funds through a single window. He believes this can avoid the duplicated investment under the traditional model, in which distributors must connect with multiple fund companies one by one, each conducting its own due diligence and system integration, saving manpower, development, and time costs while lowering the barrier to participation. Specifically, the platform provides standardized due diligence files to participating distributors and fund companies, so distributors need not review each company and each fund individually but can rely on the platform for centralized review; fund companies can likewise complete evaluation of distributors in one go through the platform.
 Leung added that the standardized services are expected to create a "triple win," simultaneously improving efficiency for fund managers, distributors, and transfer agents in data receipt, order transmission, and settlement processes, and consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading global wealth management center. He believes that with lower market barriers, small and medium-sized brokerages will find it easier to launch fund sales businesses.
 On the scale of platform participation, HKEX noted that since the launch of the order transmission service, participants have grown from an initial 33 to more than 60 distributors, fund companies, and transfer agents, with the full list published on the HKEX website and updated regularly. This infrastructure was developed by HKEX together with the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, the SFC, and industry stakeholders, with the aim of improving Hong Kong's fund distribution ecosystem and enhancing Hong Kong's competitiveness as a regional and global wealth management hub.
 Christina Ngai, Executive Director of the Investment Products Division at the SFC, noted that with the launch of the platform and agent services, all major services of the Integrated Fund Platform are now operational, achieving an important goal. She expects the platform to create substantive value by improving market efficiency and facilitating new fund distribution partnerships, and looks forward to continued industry participation; broad adoption will help grow the platform's scale and fully realize its potential. She also said that in the long run, the Integrated Fund Platform is expected to expand fund distribution channels, enabling broader investor participation in Hong Kong's fund market and thereby attracting more diverse and sustained local and cross-border capital, consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading global wealth management center.
 Reviewing the platform's rollout timeline, HKEX first established the fund database at the end of 2024, completing information standardization and centralized management for querying by various stakeholders; in mid-2025 it launched the order transmission service, connecting distributors and transfer agents; and the agent and administrative services launched this time complete the back-end processes such as holding registration, settlement and payment, and reconciliation reports. HKEX said the platform as a whole remains in a development stage and will continue to improve and expand its functions according to industry needs.
 Platform Rollout Stage Launch Date Main Content 
 Step 1: Fund Database December 2024 Integrates information on about 2,300 SFC-authorized funds; 38 million visits as of the end of September 2026 
 Step 2: Order Transmission Service July 2025 Connects fund distributors and transfer agents, simplifying and integrating operational processes 
 Step 3: Platform and Agent Services October 28, 2026 Master distribution, agent, and administrative services, covering holding administration, payment and settlement, and reconciliation reports 
 Note: Distributors, fund companies, and transfer agents participating in the platform have grown from an initial 33 to more than 60.
 On the market impact, Hong Kong's fund distribution chain was previously fragmented, with file reviews, system interfaces, and reconciliation between distributors and fund companies largely built redundantly, resulting in high operating costs and squeezing the participation space of small and medium-sized channels. With the platform centralizing due diligence, orders, settlement, and reporting into a single infrastructure, the upfront investment for new channels is expected to decline, and fund companies' channels for reaching retail and institutional clients may also expand. For investors, if subscription and redemption processes are shortened through standardization, the efficiency of fund scheduling is expected to improve; however, actual fee rates and service differences still depend on the commercial arrangements of individual distributors and fund companies.
 It is worth noting that whether the platform's benefits can be realized hinges on the scale of adoption. Both the SFC and HKEX emphasized the importance of continued industry participation. Whether the number of participants can further expand beyond the current 60-plus and whether fund companies are willing to list more products will determine whether the network effects of the platform's centralized review and one-stop connection can take shape. In an environment of intensifying cross-border capital flows and wealth management competition, the pace of this B2B distribution infrastructure's advancement will also become an indicator for observing the competitiveness of Hong Kong's asset management industry.
